capacity_gross_kwh.notes: Canada Drives lists the 58 kWh pack for the Essential/Preferred; Hyundai US release (HMGMA) also says Standard Range went from 58.0 to 63.0 kWh. A bare capacity is recorded as gross.

capacity_usable_kwh.notes: European listing of the same 58 kWh E-GMP pack (MY21): 54.0 kWh usable. Pack is shared across markets.

chemistry.notes: EV Database: NMC cathode, pouch. Wikipedia also lists the 58 kWh pack as NMC.

nominal_voltage_class.notes: EV Database: 523 V nominal, 800 V architecture.

preconditioning.notes: Estimated: electrive (2023) and Hyundai Motor Group (2023 IONIQ 5) describe automatic navigation-triggered battery conditioning with no manual control; the 2022 service bulletin TSB 23-01-017H adds the same navigation trigger to 2022 cars by software update. Applied to the whole 2022-2024 first generation (same E-GMP hardware); later Hyundai manuals add a manual option, but nothing found says the 2022-2024 cars have it. Caveats: no source was found for 2024 specifically (extended from 2023); electrive says the feature "arrived with" the 2023 model year and reached older cars by software update, so a 2022 car without that update may have no battery conditioning.

dc_max_kw.notes: Wikipedia and EV Database both list 175 kW peak for the 58 kWh pack (European/global figure; same pack).

ac_max_kw.notes: Canada Drives (Canadian 2022 trims): "10.9 kW, standard on all models". Applied to the 2023 Preferred by carry-over (same hardware). EV Database rounds to 11 kW.
